reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence, and its key premises—linking lattice distortions to enhanced dislocation mobility, cross-slip, dynamic recovery, and improved ductility/toughness in WTaTiVZr—are specific claims about material behaviour that require experimental or computational support. No such support is provided, leaving all premises ungrounded.
premises: Equimolar WTaTiVZr exhibits enhanced lattice distortions relative to pure tungsten
Lattice distortions in multi-principal element alloys lower energy barriers for dislocation movement
Lowered energy barriers promote cross-slip and dynamic recovery
Increased dislocation mobility from cross-slip/dynamic recovery leads to lower yield strength and higher ductility/toughness
These mechanisms are dominant at ~1400°C in WTaTiVZr
